payload.name: ConcreteTermQueryExpansion
payload.description: When a question contains an abstract or superordinate term, expand the search with concrete specific terms for that category and re-search if initial results are irrelevant.
content: Identify abstract or superordinate words in the question (e.g., 'physical transformation', 'achievement', 'illness') and add concrete hyponyms or descriptors likely to appear in memory (e.g., hair, weight, tournament, injury).
If the first search returns topics unrelated to the abstract category, run additional searches using those concrete expansions before concluding no information.
Use synonyms and category members to cover different wordings of the same fact.

solves: Retrieval fails when a question uses an abstract category (e.g., 'physical transformation') but memory stores the fact with concrete words (e.g., 'dyed his hair'). This rule prompts concrete-hyponym expansion and a re-search before concluding no information. It applies to any abstract-category retrieval (appearance, achievements, health, etc.) and does not apply when the query already contains the exact concrete terms.
